newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady due to payment for bills.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady due to payment for bills.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady on Wednesday, supported by payment for a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue, dealers said.
They said lack of lenders also kept rates steady.
"Some local banks and finance houses remain short of funds and this is preventing the rates from coming off," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said said some foreign banks, which are normally lenders, were also running short.
One-week money remained at 6.80/90 percent, two-week at 7.00/10 and three-week at 7.10/20.
One-month money was at 7.25/30 percent against 7.30/35. Three-month at 7.35/40 percent and six-month at 7.40/45, were both unchanged.

Dealers said that unless Bank Negara calls for new bill or bond issues, rates were likely to be pressured by improving liquidity. There will be maturity of a 900-million ringgit long-term government bond issue on Thursday and a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue on Friday.
The overnight interbank rate is expected to trade between 5.80 and 6.50 percent on Wednesday.
It fell to 5.8/6.0 percent on Tuesday from 7.30/40 on lending by large local banks.
The overnight was expected to be supported at 5.80 percent, widely accepted as the central bank's floor rate.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were lower across the board.
At 0300 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June and September contracts were both down two points to 92.66, or an implied yield of 7.34 percent.
December was also down two at 92.65, or 7.35 percent.
